html:
The Wuikinuxv, also spelled Oweekeno, are a Wakashan-speaking people of Rivers Inlet and Owikeno Lake on the central coast of British Columbia. Their language is close to that of the Heiltsuk to their north.

Rivers Inlet once had one of the greatest sockeye salmon runs on the coast, and the Wuikinuxv lived from it and from the oolichan. In the late 1800s and early 1900s canneries were built along the inlet, and workers came from all over the coast. Disease cut the Wuikinuxv to a small number. The sockeye runs collapsed in the 1990s, a heavy blow to the people. Their neighbours to the south are the Kwakwaka'wakw.
